correctness.rationale: The frequency modulation action is free because a quadratic minus a constant cannot vanish on five distinct field points unless identically zero. Its orbit of 121 rays contains exactly six origin-normalized rays for a six-zero ray. Affine changes of support transport zero sets by an invertible frequency change and a nonzero phase. For completeness, normalize one zero at the origin. If at least four zero rows had collective rank below four, the verified rank-drop property forces all zero frequencies onto one line. On that line the prime Fourier minor theorem makes four distinct samples have rank min(4, number of distinct quadratic fiber values). Rank drop therefore forces exactly three fiber values, of sizes 2,2,1, and vanishing at all four samples forces all fiber sums to vanish, contradicting the singleton's nonzero coefficient. Thus every relevant ray is seeded by four independent rows. Its full zero set determines that ray, so set deduplication is valid. An independent enumeration checked every triple for every affine representative, using reduction at the order-11 root 26 modulo 65539 as a one-sided filter and exact signed 4-by-4 cyclotomic minors for every surviving case. Every rank drop survives that filter; none is off-line. Exact origin-normalized six-zero counts are 60,30,150,0,30,0 in table order. There are full-support five-zero sets in each orbit, and no seven-or-more-zero sets, so all six maxima follow even without importing the reported external sharp bound. The orbit sizes and 121/6 conversion give the stated 532400 total.
residual_risks: This is an exact computer-assisted census at p=11 with support exactly five, not a theorem for other fields or support sizes. The independent replay uses the prime Fourier minor theorem for the collinear case.

evidence: The v1 odd-support theorem and five-point theorem give at most six at p=11. Proposition 4.11 gives a sharp example on {0,1,2,3,4}. The quoted v2 general estimate p+2 floor(k/2)-2 is 13 here, not the source of the sharp bound.

value.rationale: At the first field size in this five-point equality question beyond the analogous F7 census, the known sharp bound leaves a substantive structural question: do all shapes attain it, and with what equality multiplicities? The answer separates four attaining affine shapes from two nonattaining ones, with materially different counts among the attaining shapes. This is exact equality data for a motivated Fourier uncertainty problem, not a new computation of the already known ceiling or an isolated arbitrary witness.
residual_risks: Does not characterize equality in other primes or establish a general formula for counts.
